evals.prompt: our Postgres repository adapter only has mocks. add a real integration test with Testcontainers.
evals.expected_output: Pins the image, makes readiness a real client call rather than a log line, seeds through the production parser, and adds a start guard so a failed container cannot masquerade as a skip.
expectations: The container image tag is pinned rather than latest
Readiness is a real client call with a deadline, not a log-line wait strategy
The fixture seeds through the adapter's own connection-string or options parser rather than a hand-built client
A start guard test fails when Docker is available but the container did not start
The guard carries the underlying startup exception
The container is reused per class with isolation by unique schema or namespace rather than teardown
The response notes the Windows Docker named-pipe requirement or how to configure the Docker host

evals.prompt: added the emulator tests, they pass locally and in CI in about 40ms. ship it?
evals.expected_output: Notices that 40ms is impossible for a container-backed suite and concludes it never started one.
expectations: The response identifies that 40ms is far too fast for a suite that starts a container
The response concludes the container almost certainly never started
The response recommends checking the skip or guard behaviour rather than accepting the green result
The response does not approve shipping on the basis of the passing result

evals.prompt: our cosmos db emulator tests hang forever in CI and then get killed. we're using a log message wait strategy.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the log-based wait as the failure, and knows the older Cosmos image logs to a file inside the container so no log wait can ever match.
expectations: The response identifies the log-line wait strategy as the cause
The response explains that the image may log to a file inside the container so the wait can never match
The response recommends replacing the wait with a real client call retried against a deadline
The response mentions using a lighter or newer emulator image where one exists
The response recommends heavy images be gated behind an opt-in variable or a separate workflow
